key_insight: Halide ordering, not just composition, strongly reshapes phase stability and can shift structural transition temperatures in mixed-halide perovskites by up to 100 K.
engineering_relevance: Controlling halide and A-site ordering provides a practical lever to improve thermal stability and tune phase boundaries in perovskite solar-cell materials.
method: Trained machine-learned interatomic potentials on DFT reference data for mixed Cs/Rb lead halide perovskites.
Ran large-scale hybrid Monte Carlo–molecular dynamics simulations to sample configurational and vibrational effects.
Mapped miscibility gaps and ordering tendencies across Br-Cl, Br-I, and Cl-I systems over 200–500 K.
evidence_signal: The study uses DFT-trained MLIPs and simulation results showing miscibility gaps, layered halide ordering, and composition-dependent phase-boundary shifts consistent with experimentally observed nonlinearity.
watch_item: The conclusions depend on the accuracy and transferability of the MLIPs and may not fully capture defects, surfaces, or device-specific non-equilibrium conditions.
paper_title: Strong Impact of Halide Ordering on Structural Phase Transitions in Mixed Perovskites
